events_chronological: An immigrant shopkeeper named Nadir and his daughter Sahar buy a handgun while the dealer mocks the way he speaks.
Trey and Kwame carjack the prosecutor Halstead's car outside a restaurant.
Officer Boyle pulls over the Hobarts, gropes Renee in front of her husband Clay, and lets them go with a warning.
Boyle's partner Voss asks their commander for a new patrol car rather than keep riding with a racist.
Locksmith Mateo changes the Halsteads' locks while Paula loudly assumes he is a gang member about to sell her keys.
Mateo replaces the lock on Nadir's shop and warns him the door itself is broken, and Nadir accuses him of running a con.
Boyle pleads with a health insurance clerk, Delia Frank, for treatment for his father and is refused.
Nadir's shop is smashed and looted overnight, and the insurer refuses to pay because he ignored the warning about the door.
Renee is trapped upside down in a burning wreck and Boyle, the officer who assaulted her, crawls in and drags her out.
Trey and Kwame run down a shopkeeper named Pham and dump him outside a hospital.
Clay is stopped mid-carjacking of his own car and Voss talks the other officers out of shooting him.
Clay drives Trey away from the police at speed and then throws him out of the car.
Nadir waits outside Mateo's house with the gun and fires just as Mateo's small daughter Rosie runs into his arms.
The child is untouched - Sahar had bought blanks - and Nadir decides she is his angel.
Voss picks up Kwame hitchhiking, misreads him reaching into his pocket, shoots him dead and burns the car.
Detective Isaiah Reece is called to a body dumped by the roadside and finds that it is his brother Kwame.
Reece's mother blames him for never once going to look for his brother.
Paula falls down her stairs and tells her housekeeper Alba that she is the only friend she has.
Trey finds Pham's van packed with trafficked migrants and turns them loose at the docks instead of selling them.
In the first snow of the year another collision starts another argument in the street.
nonlinear_category_reason: A forward day-by-day chronicle into which one genuine later scene, the discovery of the body, is spliced as the opening and reached again near the end.
syuzhet_notes: The film opens on told-order bullet 1, a scene from near the end of the story, then a title card announces that what follows happened the day before, and the rest runs as a largely forward-moving braid of intercut strands. The opening moment recurs in the last act at the point where the film catches up with it, so the discovery of the body is both the first and the sixteenth thing the audience sees.
fabula_notes: The strands overlap rather than following one another and the film offers almost no time markers, so the ordering within a given day is inferred from causal links - the shop is looted after the warning, the rescue follows the traffic stop. That the body in the opening scene is the detective's brother is withheld and only becomes legible in retrospect.

events.content: He fits the new lock, then tells the shopkeeper that the lock was never the problem and that the door itself needs replacing. The shopkeeper hears a man inventing a second job for himself and orders him out.

reader: the warning that would have saved the shop is refused as a con

events.content: He sits across a desk pleading for a referral for an old man who cannot pass water without weeping, gets a flat no from the clerk, and loses it entirely at the name on her badge.

events.content: The door comes off its hinges in the night exactly as predicted. The stock is destroyed, the walls are written on, and the insurer reads the file and declines on the grounds that he was warned about the door.

Nadir: he has lost everything and is not going to be paid
reader: the refused warning becomes the reason the claim fails

events.content: The stolen car catches a small man crossing between parked vans and folds him over the bonnet. They argue about it for two streets and then leave him breathing outside a hospital entrance.

events.content: A man is dragged out of his own car at gunpoint by four officers who have been told it is stolen, and he decides, loudly, that he has had enough. One officer walks into the middle of it and gets him home.

events.content: Nothing happens. The child is not marked and neither is her father, and it comes out afterwards that the daughter, asked to buy a box of ammunition, had quietly bought the box that does nothing.

Nadir: the child is an angel and he has been spared

events.content: He picks up a young man walking in the rain, and they get on, and then a hand goes into a pocket for something and the officer who asked for a different partner puts two rounds into him and drives the body out to a ditch and burns the car.

reader: the man who thought he was the exception kills on the same reflex

events.content: A detective is called out to a body face down in the mud by a roadside, walks over with his hands in his pockets, and then stops, because he knows the shoes.

events.content: She goes over on the top step with nobody in the house and lies there until her housekeeper finds her, and in the ambulance she says, to the only person who came, that she is the best friend she has.

Paula: the person she has been rude to for years is the only one who came

events.content: He buys the wrecked van cheap, opens the back expecting stock, and finds two dozen people sitting in the dark who have been paid for. He drives them to the docks, gives them what is in his pocket and tells them to go.

reader: the man they ran over was trafficking people, and the man who ran him over lets them out

events.content: Snow starts over the city for the first time that winter. Two cars touch at a junction, both drivers get out, and the shouting starts before either of them has looked at the damage.

reader: the whole thing starts again in the next street, with different people
